chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The charity of a loaf of bread is better than a ritual (offering of) a thin (animal).'

key_terms.مَهْزُولَة: Thin or weak (referring to the sacrificial animal)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the charity of bread and a sacrificial animal in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes that the quality of the giver's intent and the practical benefit of the charity outweigh the ritualistic formality of a sacrifice. Scholars note that 'nusk mahzula' refers to an animal that is thin or weak, suggesting that a humble, sincere act of feeding the poor is spiritually superior to a potentially ostentatious or less meaningful ritual offering. This aligns with the Shia emphasis on the inner state (ikhlas) over outward appearances in acts of worship.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Giving a loaf bread in charity is better than a ritual (offering of) a thin (animal)’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has narrated from his ancestors who have said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Giving as charity one loaf is better than an emaciated offering.’”
